qc.label_under_test: Weak, dense hum (11% of tokens reach 0.1 of a small max) that rises (about 0.3-0.55) on the vocabulary and settings of talking therapies: counsellor/counselling, therapist, psychiatrist, psychologist, psychoanalyst, psychodynamic/psychotherapy, group therapy, support groups, and also speech therapy (0.33-0.46). A crisis followed by 'weekly sessions' already lifts it before any profession is named. A plain paraphrase of talking about feelings with no care words stays near baseline (0.16), as do 'retail therapy', physical medicine (surgery, dentistry, nursing, vets) and cardiology (0.06-0.2). Lateness: lowercase 'found out / realised / discovered too late that ...' stays at baseline (0.08-0.17, not peaking on ' late'), so the earlier discovered-too-late clause did not replicate; only the capitalised headline 'Too Little too Late?' (0.35) carries a late signal. The spelling-piece feeders (ap/ag/pend/sp|ät) leave no lateness meaning here: German 'Verspätung' is near zero.

neighbours.label: Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care and psychiatry in general, not only talking therapy: psychiatrist/psychologist, psychiatric hospital, antidepressant prescriptions, ECT, hallucinations / hearing voices, clinical, bipolar and postnatal depression (about 0.3-0.65). Physical-medicine twins (cardiology, burns, chemotherapy, fractures, infections) stay lower (0.1-0.3). Side channels: the '-therapist/therapy' word family lifts it even off-topic (physiotherapist 0.35, speech therapy 0.46), and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline; some disorder names alone (OCD, PTSD, anorexia, delusions) stay near the hum (0.13-0.22).

The ward treated people with severe burns who needed skin grafts.

Patients with rheumatoid arthritis often find their fingers stiff and swollen in the morning.

predictions: Expect a hold but narrow: fire median about 0.4, one near miss (burns ward) near 0.30. All sentences were probed during design on the resident model; the physiotherapist twin (0.35) was moved into the label as a side channel rather than tested as a near miss. Neighbour context: the mapped feeders/readers are name and spelling-piece units, which explain odd top hits (Sch|uh|mann, Frogg|att) but add no meaning.
